Underground Heroes and Vigilantes.text: Underground heroes are licensed professionals who avoid publicity on purpose. They turn down interviews, skip merchandise deals, work mostly at night or undercover and rarely appear near the top of the Hero Billboard Chart JP. Their work is surveillance, tracking, infiltration and the capture of villains who would see a famous face coming. Obscurity is part of the method: a villain who does not know a hero's Quirk cannot plan against it. The public barely knows their names, while the police and other pros know them well. Fans tend to think of them as eccentrics; inside the profession they are respected. Vigilantes are a different matter. A vigilante is anyone who acts as a hero without a license: patrolling, stopping crimes or fighting villains on their own authority. Under hero law that is a crime, even when the vigilante means well and even when the rescue succeeds, and the police treat vigilantes as offenders to be identified and arrested. The public is split. Some admire vigilantes as brave people filling gaps the heroes leave, especially in neighborhoods with few agencies, and every few years a local vigilante becomes an online celebrity. Others see dangerous amateurs whose fights wreck streets and get people hurt. Heroes generally side with the law, since the licensing system exists to keep untrained people from fighting in public, and good intentions do not reduce the risk.
